title: Rivergate and Summit
premise: Sebastian Thornbury, a storm chaser deep in debt to the Vane Syndicate—creditors whose relentless optimism is more frightening than any threat—takes a job from her old rival, Odile Marchetti: guide an expedition into the Rivergate basin, a place Sebastian's former crew swore off after a disaster that killed one of their own and erased another's memory. In the basin the team uncovers a buried research station whose recordings reveal the disaster was no accident, and that Sebastian herself signed off on the fatal decision before wiping her own recollection of it. As the Syndicate closes in to seize the station's findings, Sebastian must choose between protecting her found family with silence or telling the truth that could shatter it. She chooses truth, pays her debt by surrendering the station's most valuable data, and leads the expedition home—no longer invisible, but no longer hiding either.
about_author: J. M. Sandoval is the pen name of a former field researcher who spent a decade chasing weather across the Great Plains before turning to fiction. They write adventure stories about people who run toward danger and away from themselves.

chapters.title: The Optimists' Ledger
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Chasing a supercell across the plains to earn quick money, she returns to find the Vane Syndicate's cheerful enforcer waiting with a revised, worse debt figure. The emotional beat is the claustrophobia of owing everything to people who smile while they tighten the noose, establishing why she can't refuse the next offer, whatever it is.

chapters.title: An Offer from Odile
chapters.summary: Odile Marchetti, Sebastian's old rival, appears at a roadside diner with a contract: guide a funded expedition into the Rivergate basin, a region Sebastian's old crew swore off after the Kestrel disaster. Sebastian refuses, then sees the payment figure. POV alternates between Sebastian and her loyal navigator, Wren, who quietly wants her to say yes. Beat: temptation wearing a familiar face.

chapters.title: The Sworn-Off Map
chapters.summary: Sebastian assembles a small crew—Wren, mechanic Dov, and reluctant meteorologist Ilsa—while burning her copy of the old Rivergate route, only to find Odile already has it. Flashbacks hint at the Kestrel disaster without revealing details. Beat: the past refusing to stay buried, and the first fracture of trust between Sebastian and Wren.

chapters.title: Into the Basin
chapters.summary: The expedition enters Rivergate through a storm window only Sebastian can read. The land is wrong: dead instruments, unseasonal fog, a river that runs uphill in places. Odile's hired specialists grow secretive. Beat: wonder curdling into unease as the basin begins to feel less like a place and more like a memory that doesn't want visitors.

chapters.title: What the River Kept
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The team discovers a buried research station beneath the riverbank, intact and powered. Inside are recordings from the Kestrel expedition—the one Sebastian's old crew never spoke of. Wren watches Sebastian's face as she recognizes the voices on the tapes. Beat: loyalty tested by curiosity; Wren must decide whether to press or protect.

chapters.title: Sebastian, Before
chapters.summary: The recordings reveal the truth: the Kestrel deaths followed a launch call Sebastian signed, after which she underwent an elective memory wipe to survive what she'd done. She confronts Odile, who admits she knew all along—the expedition was funded by someone who wanted the station's data, and Sebastian was the key that opened it. Beat: the floor giving way beneath the protagonist's self-image.

chapters.title: The Syndicate Arrives
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. The Vane Syndicate's crews arrive by air—her debt was never money; it was her expertise, and Odile sold them access. The basin's storms, agitated by the station's machinery, trap everyone. Dov is injured securing the vehicles. Beat: all debts come due at once, and the found family closes ranks around Sebastian despite the lie she carried.

chapters.title: The Choice at Kestrel Ridge
chapters.summary: Climax. With the station flooding and the Syndicate closing in, Sebastian can escape with the data—her debt cleared, her past erased again—or broadcast the full recordings, exposing the truth and herself. She broadcasts everything, then leads the crew through the collapsing basin in a storm run only she could navigate. Beat: choosing truth over invisibility at the cost of everything she was hiding behind.

chapters.title: Debt Paid in Full
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. In the aftermath, the Syndicate, exposed and outmaneuvered, releases Sebastian—the broadcast made her more valuable as a free legend than a bound asset. Odile leaves without apology but with a grudging nod. The crew tends Dov's recovery. Beat: the strange lightness of having nothing left to hide, and the cost of it settling in.

chapters.title: Home by the Long Road
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. The expedition drives home the slow way, storms at their backs. Sebastian tells Wren the last of what she remembers of the old crew—the parts no recording held. They are not the family they were, but they are one still. Beat: resolution and quiet hope; she carries a compass, a truth, and, for the first time, no debt at all.
